entries.title: Psalms 6:1
segments: Written by David under the pressure of deep and long continued suffering, which had its origin in the persecutions to which he was exposed,

, but which seems to have reduced his body to a weak and languishing state. 
 
  Rebuke me not in thine anger; though David's enemies are persecuting him wrongfully, he yet humbly acknowledges the hand of God chastening him through them for his sons. 
 
Confidence in God, and a disposition to look to him for help, and place their hope in his mercy.

entries.title: Psalms 6:2
segments:
My bones; my whole frame. 
 
  Are vexed; filled with great distress.

entries.title: Psalms 6:3
segments: How long? wilt thou continue to afflict me?

entries.title: Psalms 6:5
segments:
For in death there is no remembrance of thee; at death all our opportunities of praising God on earth cease. 
 
The friends of God value life mainly for the opportunities it affords of honoring him and laboring in his cause.

entries.title: Psalms 6:8
segments: Great trials, borne with submission, and removed in answer to prayer, are often followed by gladness and exceeding joy.

entries.title: Psalms 6:9
segments: Receive my prayer;  hear, and answer me in mercy.
